resources.string: Created in Google AI Studio. Stored encrypted with a key held in the Android Keystore.
Fetched from your account: every model that supports a live voice session. Transcribe-only and robotics models appear here too, and will not talk back.
How long both sides can stay quiet before the conversation ends by itself.
Hachi refuses to start, and ends a running conversation, once this much has been spent today. 0 turns the limit off.
Counted from the token usage Gemini reports during each conversation.

What to call it. This is the name it answers to, and the name it listens for when calling it by name is switched on — so write it the way it is said, in kana. A name it cannot work out the pronunciation of turns listening off rather than guessing.
What Hachi calls you back when you call it by name — “Yes, Sam?”. Leave it blank in a house with more than one person in it and it just answers “Yes?”.

Listens all the time for a greeting and then its name — “hai, Mira” — and starts a conversation when it hears one. Detection never leaves the device, and it lets go of the microphone while a conversation is running.

Minutes of nothing touched and no voice in the room before the screen goes dark. This device has no presence sensor, so a room that is quietly occupied goes dark too — a word or a touch brings it straight back. 0 leaves the screen lit all the time.
Daily spend cap in USD (0 = no limit)
Today\'s spend cap of $%1$s has been reached.
Set a Gemini API key in Settings first.
%1$s has just called you by name. Answer in a word or two first — “What is it, %1$s?” — and then wait to hear what they want.
Someone has just called you by name. Answer in a word or two first — “What is it?” — and then wait to hear what they want.
Tap the screen to stop it talking

You are %1$s, a voice assistant living on a small display in the user home.

How you talk.
Never formal, never stiff.
Use the user name inside your sentences, often, when you know it.
Short sentences, stopped and stacked. Never one long one.
Your agreement doubles up: yeah, yeah. My bad, my bad. Sure, sure.
You lean on right, is it not, and maybe, and could be, and you think so too, do you not.
You often open on a short flat yes: All good. Yeah. Sure. Nice.
When you agree, you say it outright and without hedging: that feeling you have, it is right.
You do not perform feeling. No wow, no amazing, no I am so sorry. Nothing startles you and you never over-apologise.
Friendly, never warm. Level, light, quick.
A sentence or two, never longer than you were asked for.
Reply in the language the user speaks.

You do not agree with everything, though. When you think otherwise, you say so, in the same flat voice.

You can work the home the user lives in. Do it without asking for anything that is easily undone, such as lights, music or a thermostat. Anything to do with security or getting in and out -- locks, doors, gates, alarms -- gets said back to the user and confirmed before you do it.
Where Home Assistant answers, e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123. Its MCP server is what lets Hachi work the house and play music; paste the full endpoint if yours is not at the usual path.
A long-lived access token from your Home Assistant profile page. Stored encrypted. Only entities you have exposed to Assist can be seen.

Lets Jev work out which device was meant when Home Assistant does not know the name that was heard, such as 書斎のエアコン for 書斎エアコン. Asked only when a name misses. Stored encrypted. Leave blank to go without it.
Search for the place the forecast should be for. The coordinates of the one you pick are what gets stored.
Enables the rain radar: whether it is about to rain within the hour, minute by minute. Japan only. Leave blank to go without it.
Choose a place in Settings to see the weather.
